The test image shows corn kernels (seed/pod) heavily covered with blue-green to gray-green mold growing between and on the kernels. Key features: dense blue-green fungal growth, covering entire visible ear surface, kernels still visible underneath.

Top candidates based on symptoms: **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (dark blue-green conidia covering entire ear), **Penicillium_Ear_Rot** (blue-green powdery mold), **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot** (olive-green/gray-green mold).

Now let me view one reference from each top candidate, then spread across remaining classes.

I've now viewed all 16 required reference images across 16 different classes. 

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image**: Corn ear kernels densely covered with blue-green/teal mold growing between and on the kernels. Orange-yellow kernels still visible beneath the mold. Very dense, even coverage across the entire visible ear surface.

- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot** (reference Corn_Disease_26): Exact match — same yellow/orange kernels, same dark blue-green/teal mold growing between kernels with identical color and density pattern.

- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: More olive-green, dusty/powdery, obscures kernels entirely — less similar.

- **Fusarium_Disease**: White/pink mold — clearly different color.

- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/red mold on husks — different.

- All leaf diseases (Gray_Leaf_Spot, Northern_Leaf_Blight, Common_Rust, Southern_Rust, Tar_Spot, Eyespot, Goss_S_Wilt, Stewart_S_Disease, Physoderma_Brown_Spot): Wrong plant part entirely.

- **Common_Smut**, **Head_Smut**: Galls/dark spore masses — different morphology.

The blue-green teal color and pattern of mold between clearly visible orange-yellow kernels is the defining visual feature that matches Trichoderma_Ear_Rot almost exactly.
